To move your emails from Mozilla Thunderbird into a Gmail account, the simplest built-in approach is connecting Gmail to Thunderbird via IMAP and copying your folders over. However, if you have orphaned Thunderbird MBOX files or want to manage, filter, or convert your mailbox data without installing Thunderbird, using a dedicated utility like Recoveryfix Free MBOX Converter is a great alternative.

Method 1: Import Thunderbird Emails to Gmail via IMAP (Manual)

Gmail supports IMAP synchronization, allowing you to link your Gmail account inside Thunderbird and copy your existing messages directly into the cloud. 1. Enable IMAP in Gmail. Open Gmail in your browser, go to Settings (gear icon) > See all settings > Forwarding and POP/IMAP, select Enable IMAP, and click Save Changes. 2. Add Gmail to Thunderbird. Open Mozilla Thunderbird, navigate to Account Settings > Account Actions > Add Mail Account. 3. Authenticate via OAuth2. Enter your name and Gmail address, then click Continue. Thunderbird will detect Gmail's IMAP settings (imap.gmail.com, port 993, SSL/TLS). Complete the Google sign-in prompt and grant Thunderbird permission to access your account. 4. Copy Emails to Gmail. Once your Gmail folders appear in the left pane, open your local Thunderbird folder, select the messages you want to transfer (press Ctrl + A to select all), right-click, and choose Copy To > [Your Gmail Address] > [Destination Folder]. Tip: If you have a massive mailbox, copy emails in smaller batches to avoid hitting Google's IMAP bandwidth and connection limits.

What errors?

I guess I should create a new Local Folder "Old emails sent from example.com", then select all Sent messages, and move them to Local Folders > Old emails sent from example.com.

I'd rather copy those messages, as moving would also remove them from the server. Deleting from the server should be the very last thing to do, and only once the messages have been succesfully copied to the Local Folders account.

Having said that, to be able to copy messages from an IMAP account to the Local Folders account, you either still need access to the old IMAP server, or an offline copy of those messages on your local disk. Without that, there is nothing Thunderbird can copy to Local Folders.
